title: Check outgoing Engram idempotency keys are well formed and freeze how retained keys replay
outcome: Every idempotency key TermAl sends on the Engram host channel passes one producer-side well-formedness check (charset and byte length named in one contract). Keys retained in durable state and resent on replay follow a frozen, documented contract, so Engram w-e0e8bb1cfd18 can tighten its acceptance without breaking replays.
acceptance: One TermAl function owns the well-formedness rule for outgoing Engram idempotency keys: an allowed character set and a maximum byte length that Engram's current acceptance also admits. Every request constructor on the Engram host channel calls it before sending. A key that fails is refused locally with a typed error naming the request kind and is never sent.

Every current producer is covered: the checkpoint key with its observation and evidence suffixes, the verification bind key, the source-root bind, the named-root binding, termal-observe, and the evaluate and begin keys. Tests at the longest real inputs show each one passes the rule, and a test shows an over-long or out-of-charset key is refused before the send.

A written contract (docs, cross-linked from the Engram control feature brief) freezes how retained keys replay. A key persisted by an earlier build is resent byte-identical, with its original request, and is never recomputed or re-validated into a different key. Tests show a retained key that passed the rule when it was written replays unchanged after restart.
